concepts.name: Recursive base case and progress
concepts.description: Define when recursion stops and ensure every recursive call moves to a strictly smaller or simpler subproblem.

concepts.name: Recursive decompose/combine
concepts.description: Express a hierarchical problem as the same problem on child substructures, then combine child results into the parent result.

concepts.name: Tree DFS return state
concepts.description: Choose the smallest value each subtree must return so the parent can compute its own answer.

concepts.name: Tree traversal order
concepts.description: Choose preorder, inorder, or postorder according to whether parent work happens before, between, or after child work.

concepts.name: Tree breadth-first levels
concepts.description: Use a FIFO frontier to visit tree nodes by depth and preserve level boundaries when the output is distance-from-root based.

concepts.name: Binary-search-tree ordered search
concepts.description: Use the BST ordering invariant to choose one child subtree and discard the other during key search or ordered queries.

concepts.name: Trie prefix path
concepts.description: Represent string keys character by character so shared prefixes reuse the same path and prefix queries stop at the prefix node.

concepts.name: Trie terminal marker
concepts.description: Distinguish a complete stored key from a prefix path by recording whether a trie node terminates a key.

concepts.name: Trie prefix query
concepts.description: Use the node reached by a prefix as the frontier for autocomplete, prefix enumeration, or longest-prefix style lookups.

questions.prompt: A directory-size helper recursively returns the number of nodes in each subtree. What should the call return when the child reference is empty?
questions.explanation: An empty subtree contains zero nodes, so returning 0 makes the parent formula `1 + left_count + right_count` work without a special combine case.
hints: Choose the identity value that contributes nothing to a node count.

error_codes.description: The selected base-case value does not fit the subtree node-count contract.

source_refs.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 6.006 — Lecture 6: Binary Trees, Part 1

choice_feedback.zero: Correct: empty subtree contributes zero nodes.
choice_feedback.one: Returning 1 would count a missing node.
choice_feedback.none: None would require special arithmetic handling instead of matching the subtree-count contract.
choice_feedback.inf: Infinity has no useful meaning for counting nodes.

choices.label: 1, treating an absent child as a real node
`None`, forcing every parent to special-case arithmetic
A sentinel larger than any real subtree

questions.prompt: A resource tree has the rule: a parent may be deleted only after all descendants are deleted. Which traversal order naturally enforces that dependency?
questions.explanation: Postorder processes child subtrees before the parent, matching the deletion dependency directly.

source_refs.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 6.006 — Lecture 6: Binary Trees, Part 1

choice_feedback.post: Correct: descendants are handled before their parent.

questions.prompt: A CLI index changes occasionally but handles very frequent prefix-completion queries such as `kub...`. Which structure directly turns the typed prefix into a path/frontier for completions?

error_codes.description: The selected structure does not directly represent shared prefix paths.

choice_feedback.trie: Correct: shared prefixes are explicit paths.
choice_feedback.set: A hash set is excellent for exact membership but does not inherently expose prefix descendants.

questions.prompt: A trie contains the full key `apple` but NOT the full key `app`. After walking characters `a → p → p`, what additional state determines whether `app` itself is stored?
questions.explanation: The path only proves that `app` is a prefix of at least one stored key. A terminal/value marker at the node distinguishes whether `app` is itself a complete stored key.
hints: Path existence and full-key existence are not the same fact.

error_codes.description: The selected state does not distinguish a prefix-only node from a complete stored key.

choice_feedback.terminal: Correct: the terminal marker distinguishes a complete key from a prefix-only path.
choice_feedback.children: Having children only proves longer keys may continue from this prefix.
choice_feedback.depth: Depth tells key length consumed, not whether that prefix was registered as a key.
choice_feedback.sort: Sorting sibling edges does not indicate exact-key membership.
